skill.name: cloudflare-email-service
skill.description: Send and receive transactional emails with Cloudflare Email Service (Email Sending + Email Routing). Use when building email sending (Workers binding or REST API), email routing, Agents SDK email handling, or integrating email into any app — Workers, Node.js, Python, Go, etc. Also use for email deliverability, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, wrangler email setup, MCP email tools, or when a coding agent needs to send emails. Even for simple requests like "add email to my Worker" — this skill has critical config details.
skill.summary: Build Cloudflare transactional email sending, routing, deliverability, and agent integrations.
skill.author: cloudflare

security_audit.summary: All 74 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, documented official API calls, Worker handler syntax, or Durable Object SQL APIs. Semantic review found three medium concerns involving untrusted email content, unescaped HTML replies, and sensitive message logging. No malicious prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or arbitrary process execution was found.

remediation.issue: Inbound email can be supplied to an AI agent without explicit trust boundaries.
remediation.suggestion: Treat message content as untrusted data, isolate it from instructions, restrict agent tools, and require approval before sending replies or taking external actions.

remediation.issue: The reply example interpolates replyBody directly into HTML.
remediation.suggestion: Escape text before creating HTML, or sanitize allowed markup with a maintained HTML sanitizer before sending the message.

remediation.issue: The parsing example logs complete inbound subject and body values.
remediation.suggestion: Log identifiers and delivery metadata only. Redact personal data, credentials, links, and message content before any diagnostic logging.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Email Content Can Reach an AI Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The guide stores inbound email text and suggests notifying an AI agent to draft replies without defining an untrusted-content boundary. Crafted email text could attempt indirect prompt injection before the agent uses reply capabilities.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide explicitly combines stored inbound content with optional AI drafting. The agent call is illustrative and commented, so exploitability depends on the implementation.

semantic_findings.title: Reply Content Is Inserted Into HTML Without Escaping
semantic_findings.description: The reply example inserts replyBody directly into an HTML template. Untrusted or AI-generated markup could alter outgoing email content or add tracking and phishing elements.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The direct interpolation into the HTML field is visible in the example, and no escaping or sanitization step is shown.

semantic_findings.title: Inbound Email Contents Are Written to Logs
semantic_findings.description: The parsing example logs the full subject and text of incoming messages. Email bodies can contain personal data, reset links, or secrets that should not enter routine logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example directly passes parsed subject and body text to console.log. The exposure is clear, although retention and access depend on deployment settings.

content.value_statement: Transactional email setup is easy to misconfigure across Workers, REST APIs, and routing. This skill provides current patterns for sending, receiving, authentication, and deliverability.
actual_capabilities: Configures Email Sending bindings for Cloudflare Workers.
Builds transactional email requests with Workers bindings or the REST API.
Implements inbound Email Routing handlers for forwarding, rejecting, parsing, and replying.
Guides Agents SDK integrations for receiving and replying to email.
Explains Wrangler and MCP workflows for domain setup and sending.
Reviews SPF, DKIM, DMARC, suppression lists, analytics, and delivery practices.
limitations: Requires a Cloudflare account and an onboarded sending domain.
Does not replace current Cloudflare documentation for changing APIs or limits.
Does not provide a bulk marketing or newsletter platform.
Does not operate Cloudflare resources without user credentials and approval.

use_cases.title: Add Transactional Email
use_cases.description: Configure a Worker binding and send account notifications with plain-text and HTML content.

use_cases.title: Build an Inbound Support Mailbox
use_cases.description: Route incoming messages to a Worker, parse them, store them, and prepare reviewed replies.

use_cases.title: Improve Delivery Health
use_cases.description: Check authentication records, suppression handling, sending limits, and analytics for a production email domain.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a Worker Binding
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Cloudflare Email Sending to my Worker. Show the Wrangler configuration and a basic transactional welcome email with text and HTML.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for an existing Worker

prompt_templates.title: Send Through the REST API
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Cloudflare Email Service REST request for my external application. Use environment-based credentials and explain the response states.

prompt_templates.title: Process Incoming Email
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Email Routing handler that parses one raw message, validates the sender, stores metadata, and forwards only to verified destinations.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Reviewed AI Mailbox
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a secure support mailbox using Email Routing, Durable Objects, and an AI drafting agent. Include prompt-injection controls, approval, sanitization, and observability.

output_examples.input: Add transactional welcome emails to my Cloudflare Worker.
output: Add an EMAIL sending binding to the Worker configuration.
Verify the sending domain before deployment.
Send both plain-text and HTML content through the binding.
Handle delivery errors without exposing recipient data.

output_examples.input: Help me receive support emails and reply after review.
output: Route the support address to an email handler.
Read and parse the raw stream once.
Store structured message fields in a Durable Object.
Require user approval before sending a threaded reply.

output_examples.input: Why are messages reaching spam folders?
output: Verify SPF, DKIM, and DMARC alignment.
Review bounces, suppressions, and delivery analytics.
Use accurate subjects, complete text content, and valid unsubscribe handling where required.

best_practices: Use Workers bindings when possible and keep REST API tokens in managed secrets.
Verify sending domains and include both plain-text and HTML message bodies.
Treat inbound messages as untrusted and review agent-generated replies before sending.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode API tokens or expose them in logs and examples.
Do not use transactional email infrastructure for newsletters or unsolicited bulk messages.
Do not insert untrusted text into outgoing HTML without escaping or sanitization.

faq.question: Can this skill send email from a Cloudflare Worker?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains the Email Sending binding, domain onboarding, message fields, attachments, errors, and restricted destinations.

faq.question: Can it support applications outside Workers?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents the Cloudflare REST API and credential handling for Node.js, Python, Go, and other clients.

faq.question: Does it handle incoming email?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Email Routing handlers, forwarding, rejection, MIME parsing, storage, and threaded replies.

faq.question: Is it suitable for marketing campaigns?
faq.answer: No. Cloudflare Email Service is described here for transactional email, not newsletters or bulk marketing campaigns.

faq.question: Does it configure DNS authentication?
faq.answer: It explains onboarding and verification for SPF, DKIM, and DMARC. Actual DNS changes still require account access and user approval.

faq.question: How should AI-generated replies be secured?
faq.answer: Treat email as untrusted data, restrict agent tools, sanitize outgoing HTML, and require human approval before sending.
